text_fidelity_a:
Alienware Alpha ASM100-4980 Console (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This review is going to be a bit difficult to write in that there is SO much to say about this system that different people might be interested in knowing about. I will attempt to be as brief, yet well rounded in my review as I can due to space constraints.

WHAT IS THE ALIEN ALPHA CONSOLE (7980)?
In essence, what this unit is, is a complete Windows 8.1 PC unit with the ability to boot directly into Valve's Big Picture console interface of the Steam accounts immediately, or boot directly into Windows. No matter what, you have to be online to be able to the Steam Console because of the fact that in order to access your account, you have to be able to log in.

In order to log in, you have to be online. Big Picture mode can also be accessed through Windows. By pressing the icon for Steam on the desktop (which will take you directly into your Steam account) you can also access the Big Picture console interface by pressing the controller symbol in the top right corner of the window.

This console comes with Windows 8.1 which is a challenge in itself as the operating system has a lot of quirks and frustrations that come along with it no matter WHAT hardware it operates on. There is a bit of a learning curve with Windows 8.1 but it is worth taking the time to work with it, if you have never used it before.

The machine itself is very small- smaller than a PS3 unit. It has a cool alien head on the front of the machine that changes colors during different operations. You hook it up into your sound system through HDMI or Digital Optical Link, or into TV directly using HDMI.

The power cord is in two parts- it is 68 inches from the console to the AC adapter and 32 inches from the adapter to the plug. It also comes with a 6ft HDMI cable.

There is an HDMI IN so you can input HDMI sources to pass through this unit into your TV.

WHAT CAN YOU DO WITH THE ALIEN ALPHA CONSOLE?
This machine is set up with the gamer in mind. It is very powerful and does play some of the highest demanding games on the market right now without any trouble. It is also set up with the console gamer in mind, specifically the Xbox crowd as it comes with a wireless Xbox 360 controller (which is already set up to work in Windows).

Many Playstation gamers as well as others are not fond of this controller. We did manage to set up a Playstation 3 controller using the Motion Joy and Pinnacle Profiler method that we downloaded from online. Motion joy is free, but Pinnacle Profiler is a one-time fee to download it (after a 20 day trial period).

CAN YOU PLAY OLDER PC GAMES ON THIS SYSTEM?
One of the concerns I had, which I am sure others out there might have is- "Can I play all of my older PC games on this unit as well as Steam games?" The answer is YES! All of our games (purchased through Gog.com previously) work beautifully on this system. That means you do not have to be connected to the internet to play them.

WHAT SHOULD YOU PLAN TO PURCHASE?
--Keyboard (I use Logtiech K400 wireless w/ touchpad on board I use for basic Windows stuff)
--Mouse (I use Marathon Mouse for games)
--DVD-ROM/CD-ROM USB drive (if you want to install anything using those)
--Wireless headphones if you want to use them for gaming

BLUETOOTH
I have a pair of Turtle Beach i30 wireless headphones that operate by bluetooth. I found conflicting information on their site as to whether this would work with Windows 8.1 or not, so I tried installing it.

Windows 8.1 has some idiosyncrasies with bluetooth and is notorious for causing problems in this area. When attempting to install my headphones with this system, the process somehow completely messed up the bluetooth operations in the system. It took me a couple of days to figure it all out, but with a lot of perseverance and some Free Ccleaner added for registry and system cleaning, I managed to get the bluetooth headphones to work beautifully.

This is not a console problem but a Windows 8.1 problem.

ARMA III
We ran this game with maxed out settings, this system ran 30fps smoothly and perfectly. (At the time of this review Arma III is a military simulator that has a very high graphics demand. It is one of the top most demanding games on the market at this time.)

Graphically it looks way better than anything from Modern Warfare.

IS THIS WORTH IT?
PROS
-completely functional PC in all aspects of Windows 8.1
-small physical footprint
-plays all levels of PC games very well
-comes with Xbox controller
-works with PS3 controller
-can get decent keyboard and mouse for very little extra money
-allows family gaming
-more convenient for limited space in living area
-will shut off with front switch like console
-everyone can have their own account
-can play old PC games on this (if updated as in GOG.com purchases)
-can upgrade memory and hard drive

CONS
-expensive(but very powerful for this price range)
-need to purchase keyboard and mouse for Windows operations
-Windows 8.1 can be a bit frustrating at times (Win 8.1 is not unique to this console, however)

THE BOTTOM LINE
When I first read about this console/PC unit, I thought it was way overpriced, but after using it, I REALLY like it so far. We have put this thing through constant use and pushing it since we got it. I have to say it is up to the task. My son who is an avid gamer and builds super computers is even impressed with it, which is saying a lot. In his opinion, it is a very powerful system for the price.

This is a PC designed for console gamers who might not really have discovered the world of PC gaming yet. It seems to be a solid machine that performs well. Working with Windows is not always an easy task, but in set up and basic gaming operations this system is really impressive to me.

WHO WOULD NOT WANT TO GET THIS SYSTEM
This is a high functioning computer that will run games on it and has a console experience attached with it. If you are just interested in using this for Steam, I would say that it is not worth the money. If you want to have a highly functioning Windows 8.1 system (capable of some great gaming) that allows you to have a console experience with Steam as an added bonus all on your TV, then this system is great.

UPDATE 6-2015
We are still crazy about this system. The more that we use it, the more fun it is to explore. The Alien Respawn takes a bit of messing with to get it to work right, but after the update, I finally got the system backed up.

The Steam console has been fun to use, although again, it is quirky when trying to use the Xbox 360 controller that we got with it. There is a glitch that causes some problems occasionally and has to be re-installed from time to time. I am not sure if it is a Windows 8.1 problem or a Steam problem. We are hoping to get the Steam controller when it comes out if it looks like a solid option.

We all have gotten and use Steam accounts and found it to work well so far. We are playing on Wi-Fi (not solid line in) and it still performs quite well.

All in all, this system is FANTASTIC and I can not recommend it highly enough. If I could give it TEN stars, I would.

And as silly as it seems, having the ability to change the colors on the alien head and the triangle shape thrills me to no end. Simple but fun.

Will update if we get the Steam controller to let you know how that works.
text_fidelity_b: Alienware Alpha ASM100-4980 Console (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
SAMSUNG 55-Inch Class QLED Q60B Series - 4K UHD Dual LED Quantum HDR Smart TV with Alexa Built-in (QN55Q60BAFXZA, 2022 Model) So...

I bought the 43" QLED Q60B. Also bought the Samsung 9200S soundbar with wireless sub, and then bought their wireless rear speakers. That part is awesome, but will be a separate review.

1- Despite checking answers and even asking the Samsung Specialist about Hands Free Alexa (ie. don't press the MIC button), the 2022 version DOES NOT have this feature, which of course, after buying it, installing it 10ft up in the corner of the bedroom, and trying to make it work.... had to call Samsung directly to troubleshoot, who said it is not available after 2021. Even Bixby, which I can't stand, is grayed out.

2- Not-so-Smart. I have had a ROKU on all my other Samsung TVs because they were older. So I became accustomed to much more variety it seems. Other than the big ones, the variety is disappointing, even in the music section.

3- I do not buy a TV outright only to have the manufacturer decide what I CAN'T remove. The first damn option in your "customizing" short cut bar, is SAMSUNG'S forced-on-you advertising slot, that cannot be moved out of the or removed, and I have no interest in it! There are a few others that can't be dropped, but can be moved.

4- Despite trying to follow the trend to smaller remotes, they missed the mark. People want quick access to things. Mute should ALWAYS have it's own button, not remembering to press and hold a specific button to mute it. Your Settings access is NOT intuitive. I trying to make it easier, you somehow over-complicated it. Some items are ambiguous (maybe it's under this one?), and I find myself searching for things and when I finally find them, the controls are often limited.

It's 2022, I just bought a quality TV from a previously adored and promoted-by-me brand, and I'm super pissed. My buddy's LG is much better, and I'm now going to add a fricking Roku to a TV that is state of the art. And for a 43" I could have gotten an off-name brand with awesome pic and Roku built in, for half the price!!!! Lesson Learned!

Boo to Samsung on this. And don't send me to your useless Facebook help page when you already dropped the ball!
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG 55-Inch Class QLED Q60B Series - 4K UHD Dual LED Quantum HDR Smart TV with Alexa Built-in (QN55Q60BAFXZA, 2022 Model)

text_fidelity_a:
Canon EF 100mm f/2.8 Macro USM Fixed Lens for Canon SLR Cameras Although this lens is intended for macro photography, it's also a great lens for general purpose shots, or portrait shots. The lens produces beautiful sharp images and is a fast, accurate focuser. The lens is moderately heavy and bulky, so I wouldn't classify it as eminently carryable, and without image stabilization, you might suffer hand shake blur if you're not shooting at the wide end; at smaller apertures, using it with a tripod is highly recommended. But if you're buying it primarily to get into macro this shouldn't much matter as tripod shooting with macro is virtually a necessity, and completely expected.

The 100mm focal length is a nice compromise when you want to get close to small subjects (particularly insects) but are limited to how close you can get before scaring the subject off - as a comparison with the 180mm macro, you would want to factor in a consideration as to what you might like to shoot most of the time - big spiders that you'd rather stay well away from might be an application more suited to the 180mm, for instance, but if you are keen to shoot mostly flowers, the 180 might be more length than you really need.

In short, the 100mm macro is one of my "keeper" lenses, a real performer.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF 100mm f/2.8 Macro USM Fixed Lens for Canon SLR Cameras

text_fidelity_a:
Pogoplug Backup and Sharing Device (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Pros: If you are a beginner to computer networking and you just want to host a cloud server at home for tablet and smartphone access to your music and video library, this is the device for you. Set-up is simple, anyone who can install a Linksys router can do it, and tech support is decent (for the purposes of this review, I called and asked them to help me with a non-existent issue so I could report that they do in fact help people, then I told the guy I was a mystery shopper and thanked him for his help).

Cons: If you have Carbonite back-up service, if you have a WD MyBookLive NAS, or if you know how to configure any of the several dozen software packages that do this for you, then you can already do this for free without buying this device. Yes, I do mean that there are free packages (at least for Android phones) which you can download and use to make your computer into this device without any fees whatsoever. So for anyone who is mid-level or above in computers, this is not a worthwhile purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Pogoplug Backup and Sharing Device (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

I can adjust the Boyata Laptop Holder to the angle most comfortable for me. I can also use this to angle my screen and also use a separate keyboard and mouse (which I can store underneath when not in use). Also, this fits my LG Notebook, my 12.9" iPad Pro, my [[ASIN:B01MTGLBP5 Samsung Galaxy Tab S3 9.7"]], and my Google Nexus 7 comfortably.

Pictures 1 & 2 shows my LG Notebook front and side stand profile.
Picture 3 shows my 12.9" iPad Pro
Pictures 4 & 5 shows my 9.7" Samsung Galaxy Tab S3 in portrait and landscape
Picture 6 shows my 7" Google Nexus

Picture 8 shows my LG Notebook closed with mouse pad on top and room enough to store my mouse and LG flip phone behind it. If I were also using a wireless keyboard, I could have slipped that in the space underneath the stand.

Only time will tell if the "hinges" on this stand will last and not collapse. I suppose if one changes the position of the stand daily, that this may not be so sturdy. Nevertheless, so far I love it and am thrilled that I ordered this. If it should fail in any way, I will update my review.

UPDATE August 5, 2020 - I have been using this daily with my LG Laptop for almost two years now and it is still going strong. The stand does not collapse when I type on my laptop and it holds the keypad at the perfect angle. I would defintely order another one if I needed it.

text_fidelity_a:
HP Stream 7 32GB Windows 8.1 Tablet (Includes Office 365 Personal for One Year) I was really looking forward to trying this tablet out. To date I'd had no exposure to Windows 8.1 or a dedicated Windows tablet. I have had a decent 10.1 inch Android tablet.

First are foremost, the elephant in the room... or rather, the mouse. This is a seven inch wide screen tablet. I have friends whose who online lives are conducted via five inch cell phone screens and they're happy with it. The screen on this tablet is nice. Don't get me wrong. I was able to stream from Amazon video in HD (720) and the video was crisp and clean. Images display well but, again, the screen is just seven inches. I can't imagine trying to be productive with something so small.

For a device with only one gig of RAM this runs Windows fairly well. I wws able to load several Windows programs including the Calibrě eBook manager which took a little longer to convert eBooks between formats but did the job. I also loaded a legacy email and Usenet program that I've been using for a decade or longer. Along with directly installed programs I also downloaded a handful of apps from the very buggy Microsoft app store. The store worked less than 50% of the time while I was trying this tablet out. I at one point had to resort to switching to a local login account and then back to my Hotmail logi. It only took about an hour of reading web forums to find that solution to the Windows app store refusing to work.

Two problems I ran into were the sound which is from a single speaker hidden in a slot on one of the short sides of the tablet. If you want to listen to anything other than the default Window's beeps and tones you'll want to pair this with a blue tooth speaker or headphones. The speaker in this tablet is deplorable. The next problem I had was the tablet runs HOT. I was running a program designed for Windows 98, downloading and reading posts un Usenet and viewing a few posted vacation and astronomy images and I had to stop. The tablet was so hot it was uncomfortable to hold and I worried it might overheat and become damaged.

While I was impressed to see Windows running on a small tablet I was thoroughly unimpressed with Windows 8.1 the tile system is just terrible.

So, it has good video quality on a too small screen with horrible sound and a flaky app store to rely upon, though you can download and install normal Windows programs. I just wasn't that crazy about this tablet. And will definitely be sticking with Android and a much larger screen.
text_fidelity_b: HP Stream 7 32GB Windows 8.1 Tablet (Includes Office 365 Personal for One Year)

text_fidelity_a:
Netgear WGR614 Wireless-G Router We bought this Netgear WGR614 router back in March 2006. It installed somewhat easily and except for a little problem with the wireless PC card for the laptop (wouldn't be recognized at first but easily corrected) we had pretty stable use for about a year. Then we began to have connection problems. The connection would get slower and slower until internet pages would just not load, resulting in repeated "page cannot be displayed" errors. Powering down and restarting the router, modem and computer seemed to correct the issue. But as of this morning the router appears to have completely died. Powering down and restarting does nothing, the internet connection cannot be re-established. We can connect the desktop directly to the cable modem but for now the laptop is without connection, making for some unhappy family members here.

As of right now I don't know if we'll be buying another Netgear router & wireless PC card. The life expectancy of Netgear products does not appear to be all that great. Looking at some of the reviews we appear to be quite lucky that we got as much time out of the router as we did. Still I'm not in the mood to be shopping for a new router every 1.5 years or less. Hopefully there is a good router out there that can last at least two years.
text_fidelity_b: Netgear WGR614 Wireless-G Router

SUPCASE Galaxy Tab S3 9.7" Case Unicorn Beetle Pro Series Full-Body Rugged with Built-in Screen Protector, Blue/Black (SUP-Galaxy-TabS3-9.7-UBPro-Blue/Black) When I ordered this, I didn't realize that I would be required to use the screen protector part of it. I thought that I could just slip on the back piece and use it like that. When I realized that both pieces are required (the back is too big and wouldn't stay on without the screen protector piece; hey, it's the first time I've ordered something with an integrated screen protector, so I didn't know), I wanted to send it back without even trying it.

I'm glad that I decided to try it for a couple of days, first. The screen is always covered with fingerprints and smudges and I find myself wiping it off many times a day. It also scratches easily. Since we're all washing our hands 40 times a day, the amount of fingerprints feels excessive to me and I hate looking at it. Even so, with the screen protector on, the screen is very responsive. Zero problems. And while I'm actually using my tablet, I don't notice the scratches or fingerprints.

There is also a shimmery rainbow effect. I don't really notice it while the screen is on and it seems to be less of an effect after the couple of weeks that I've been using it. I think because there's less of an air gap.

Everything lines up perfectly and the back part of the case also seems perfect to me. I would love to see this brand make a version that's just the well-fitted back piece.

So is it perfect? No. However, the things that bother me about it aren't really noticeable while the screen is on and I'm using it. It's protective and the screen protector doesn't interfere in the responsiveness of the screen in any way. So overall, I do think that this purchase was worth it. I'm glad that I decided to try it instead of immediately sending it back.

Another comment -- I keep a little piece of electrical tape over the front camera hole. The screen protector holds the tape in place so that I don't have to periodically change it anymore.
text_fidelity_b: SUPCASE Galaxy Tab S3 9.7" Case Unicorn Beetle Pro Series Full-Body Rugged with Built-in Screen Protector, Blue/Black (SUP-Galaxy-TabS3-9.7-UBPro-Blue/Black)

The sound is pretty good, with decent bass, although BT muddles most of the high end. They stay in the ear pretty good, and the flat cord doesn't get tangled or knotty the way a typical round cord does.
What I am not happy with is the battery life. Last week I took a fully charged set of these for a 90 minute trail run, and when I was done the battery was dead. My phone was less than a foot away from the set and I didn't do any fussing with it, just put them on and went. This happens more times than not. No sure if I can return them or not, but for sound I give them a 4, but battery life a 2. Hence, my overall 3 stars.

text_fidelity_a:
Kensington Orbit Wireless Trackball with Scroll Ring - Black-Red (K70990WW), I own ALL of the kensington line of trackballs (clearly a trackball nut). From the original Expert Mouse (using a serial connection) all the way to this one. I can see how some purists are very touchy about their trackball performing and as it becomes an extension of interfacing with the computer, it's critical that it performs well.

PROS:
* Nice compact footprint; Not too demanding for space.
* Comes with the little ergonomic squishy thingy for a wrist-rest.
* The ball 'stays in' the unit even if you turn it over! This is a new concept for their trackballs! (you can pop it out if you need to condense for travel)
* Scroll wheel is nice; A feature present only in the higher-end trackballs.

CONS:
* BUTTONS! YUK! The button has some kind of contact issue where if you press it gently enough, you hear and feel a little 'click' but you didn't actuate the button! You must press it harder, and get a louder firmer CLICK! (really kinda mushy) to click it! I have tried different spots on the button and it's all the same! This is ALMOST a deal killer for me, but I'm going to give it some time, see if the button wears in and that false-click goes away over time.
* Scroll wheel is not free-flowing like on the modern expert mouse. With that sucker, you can fling the wheel and it will roll atleast for a half-second or so! This one really resists movement so it's more like a mouse-wheel than a scroll-wheel. It does not have a 'ribbed' feel, it rolls smoothly but it's not a 'on rails' as other models.

My personal favorite is still the modern expert mouse. It's massive (like a little tank on your desktop!) but you can navigate quickly with it, and use it in the manner a trackball was designed to be used.

Hope my review helps you!
text_fidelity_b: Kensington Orbit Wireless Trackball with Scroll Ring - Black-Red (K70990WW),

text_fidelity_a:
12x42 HD Binoculars for Adults with Binocular Harness Strap and Upgraded Phone Tripod and Adapter 12x42 High Definition Binoculars for Bird Watching 12x42 Binoculars for Hunting Hiking Gifts for Men These binoculars themselves are great. They seem to focus well with my glasses on, and show good detail. I have an astigmatism and don’t always do well with binoculars, so this is good. I was able to see tiny pine needles on a distant tree, for instance. The larger lenses have removable covers that stay attached to the binoculars, and the front pieces have a removable cover that comes off completely. There’s a microfiber cleaning wipe that comes with, and the glass lenses seem to be lovely quality.

The accessories are nice but cheap. First: the case. I wish it were better made, at least as well-made as the binoculars that go inside. I wish there were pockets for accessories, too. There’s a “bonus” compass with whistle, lanyard, thermometer and flashlight. There’s also a remote shutter device. Both take a #2032 button battery, which is one of the most common and easy to purchase.

I was excited about the cell phone accessory, and still am, though it’s not perfect. This accessory clamps onto the phone after one aligns the eyepiece and lens. My right two photos show indoor and outdoor examples of photos taken with this accessory. I will say that the clamp doesn’t go too wide, and doesn’t fit around my pop socket. I wish that it were a bit bigger and could accommodate these. One must hold one’s hand mighty steady using the cell phone camera with the binoculars, but it can be done. It’ll probably take me some time to fully get the hang of it. The outdoor photo was taken just before sunset.

The binoculars are solid, so the less-than-perfect-quality accessories aren’t a deal-breaker for sure, depending on price. I would recommend these, and will enjoy using them.
text_fidelity_b: 12x42 HD Binoculars for Adults with Binocular Harness Strap and Upgraded Phone Tripod and Adapter 12x42 High Definition Binoculars for Bird Watching 12x42 Binoculars for Hunting Hiking Gifts for Men
